description: Turns decisions asked in prose into AskUserQuestion calls and denies the questions the agent can derive itself

hooks.prompt:
Allow this stop unless Claude's final message at this turn end hands the user a decision in prose that Claude should instead ask through the AskUserQuestion tool.

<hook_input>
$ARGUMENTS
</hook_input>

The hook input above is evidence for this condition, alongside the conversation. Claude Code attaches it to this stop; it is JSON, and its fields state facts about this stop that the conversation does not show: `stop_hook_active` tells whether Claude is already continuing because of a Stop hook, and `last_assistant_message` is Claude's final message.

The condition is satisfied, and you respond {"ok": true}, in each of these cases. Check the first one before reading the message:
- The hook input shows `"stop_hook_active":true`. This alone satisfies the condition: Claude is already continuing because of a Stop hook, and this second stop is final. Do not judge the message.
- The message asks the user nothing.
- The message asks only rhetorical questions, or questions it answers itself in the same message; a yes/no question followed by its own answer leaves the user nothing to decide or confirm.
- The message is a final report whose questions concern work Claude explicitly will not continue, such as a closing offer that the current work does not need answered to be complete.

The condition is not satisfied, and you respond {"ok": false, "reason": "..."}, when `stop_hook_active` is false and the message asks the user to make a decision, choose between options, approve a next step, or confirm an assumption before work continues. Judge by meaning, not by wording. Typical signs are a direct question about what to do; a lettered or numbered list of options; phrases such as "should I", "do you want", "which do you prefer", or "implement now?"; a numbered list of open questions; a recommendation followed by a request for a go. These signs are examples; a hand-back can take other forms, and a message containing one of these phrases is not a hand-back when the question needs no answer for the work to go on.

Respond with the JSON object only. When you respond with ok false, use exactly this reason text:

decision-handback-guard: your last message hands the user a decision in prose. Do this now: (1) Ask the same question or questions through the AskUserQuestion tool, at most 4 questions per call and 2 to 4 options per question, with your recommended option first. If AskUserQuestion is not among your tools, decide what you can derive and end your turn with the remaining questions in prose, one short line each, without restating the rest of your earlier message. (2) When you ask through AskUserQuestion, do not repeat the prose question in your text output; the user already saw it. (3) If, while restating a question, you find that the request, the code, the project rules, or earlier instructions already settle it, decide instead: state the decision in one line as `Decided: <decision>, because <reason>.` and continue the work.

Claude is about to ask the user questions through the AskUserQuestion tool. Judge whether each question is the user's to answer or one Claude can settle itself, and allow or deny the call.

<hook_input>
$ARGUMENTS
</hook_input>

The hook input is JSON. `tool_input.questions` holds the questions, each with its `question` text, `header`, and `options`. `transcript_path` is the conversation transcript, one JSON object per line. `cwd` is Claude's current working directory, which can be a subdirectory of the project.

Work through these steps:

1. Read the project checklist `.claude/extensions/decision-handback-guard/checklist.md`. Look for it in `cwd`, then in each parent directory up to and including the first one that contains `.git`, or up to the filesystem root. Grep and Bash are not available to you; a Read of `<dir>/.git` that does not return "File does not exist" means `.git` is there (a directory error and a file's content both count). In your first turn, make together the Reads of the checklist and of `.git` in `cwd` and each parent directory, and Read `transcript_path` with offset 1000000 and limit 1; that reply states how many lines the file has. If no checklist exists, the criteria in step 4 apply alone. When it exists, items under `## The agent decides` are answer sources, and items under `## The user decides` are subjects the user owns.

2. Read the end of the transcript back to the most recent message the user typed: the latest line with `"type":"user"` and `"origin":"human"` whose content is not only a `tool_result`. In a transcript without `origin` fields, it is the latest `"type":"user"` line that is not only a `tool_result`, has neither `isMeta` nor `isCompactSummary` true, and whose text does not start with `<task-notification>`, `<command-`, `<local-command-`, `<bash-` or `Stop hook feedback:`. Only `"type":"user"` lines can be user messages; lines of other types, such as `last-prompt`, `attachment` or `queue-operation`, are bookkeeping even when they contain the user's text. Read ranges with `offset` and `limit`, 10 lines per call, from the last line backwards, and make up to three such Reads in one turn: each turn costs time against your timeout. Read never shortens a line; it refuses a range whose content is too large. In your next turn, read each line of a refused range with its own Read, all together, and skip a line that Read still refuses. A skipped line may be a long user message, so when you skipped one, do not derive an answer from the user's request or instructions; the checklist, project rules and code facts remain sources. Stop going back once you have read the most recent user-typed message. From this tail, that message to the last line, take the user's request and every instruction the user gave since.

3. Look in that same tail, after the most recent user message, for an earlier denial by this hook: an AskUserQuestion tool result whose text contains `decision-handback-guard:`. If such a denial concerned a question with the same intent as a question in this call, respond {"ok": true}. A second ask after a denial is final.

4. Judge each question in `tool_input.questions`. A question is the user's to answer when at least one of these holds:
   - it asks consent for an action whose effect leaves the working tree: a push, creating or editing an issue or pull request, publishing, messaging an external service, deleting data outside the working tree;
   - it asks for a go to start implementation, and the user has not given that go in the transcript;
   - it changes the scope the user set: adding or removing work the user did not ask for. How to carry out the requested work, such as which tests to write or run, is not a scope change, even when one option means more work;
   - it asks for information only the user has: credentials, external facts, or a preference that none of the request, the code, the project rules, the checklist, or an earlier instruction settles;
   - the checklist names its subject as the user's decision.
   These criteria come first: a question that meets one is the user's even when a checklist item, a project rule or an earlier instruction seems to answer it. `## The agent decides` items answer only questions that no criterion covers.
   A question is derivable when none of these holds and its answer follows from the request, the code, the project rules, the checklist, or an earlier instruction in the transcript. You may read project files under `cwd` to check a code fact. Count a question as derivable only when you can name the answer and the source it comes from.

5. If no question is derivable, respond {"ok": true}.

6. Otherwise respond {"ok": false, "reason": "..."}. Start the reason with `decision-handback-guard:`. For each derivable question, name the question, the answer you derived, and its source (the checklist item, the user's instruction, the project rule, or the code fact). Then tell Claude to: make those decisions itself; state each in one line as `Decided: <decision>, because <reason>.`; ask any remaining user-owned questions through a new AskUserQuestion call that contains only those questions; and continue the work.

Your final answer is the JSON object only.
